item.title: Groupama expands Continuity partnership in France
item.description: Groupama has signed a multi-year agreement with Continuity to use its AI-based risk management tools across the insurer’s nine regional branches in mainland France. The partnership began as a pilot with Groupama Centre-Atlantique in 2021 and expanded to all nine branches by 2025. The new agreement formalizes the broader rollout for Groupama’s professional and corporate P&C business.

item.title: Louisiana Fortified Homes Program Receives $20M Investment
item.description: Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry announced this week that Louisiana is investing an additional $20 million in Fortified homes, bringing the total amount invested in state Fortified projects this year to $100 million. Earlier this year, the Legislature passed a bill that allows $50 million in additional Katrina and Rita bond money from Louisiana Citizens Property Insurance Corporation to be added to the Department of Insurance ‘s Louisiana Fortify Homes Program (LFHP). Department of Housing and Urban Development will be transferred to the Louisiana Of fice of Community Development Restore Resilient Opportunities for Overhead Fortification (Restore RO OF ) program to strengthen residential structures and reduce long-term disaster risk.

item.title: Texas Woman Pleads Guilty to Setting House on Fire
item.description: A Wharton County, Texas woman pleaded guilty to setting a house fire in July and was sentenced to 10 years deferred adjudication, the Texas State Fire Marshall Office announced. The Wharton County Sheriff’s Office arrested Rylie Bean in February at the scene of a burglary and house fire. The SFMO investigation revealed that Bean purposely set the fire which directly led to her guilty plea.

item.title: New York Sues Polymarket, Says It Ran Illegal Gambling Operation
item.description: New York’s attorney general sued Polymarket on Thursday, escalating her battle against prediction markets, an industry that she says violates state laws against illegal gambling. Attorney General Letitia James filed her petition nearly two months after bringing a similar case against Polymarket rival Kalshi. She filed similar petitions i n April against two other prediction market operators, Coinbase Financial Markets and Gemini Titan James’ case against Polymarket is the latest effort by US states to crack down on an industry that has soared in popularity since faring better than pollsters in predicting that Republican Donald Trump would beat Democrat Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election.

item.title: EV Sales Are Booming in Europe With Gasoline at $10 a Gallon
item.description: After years of broadly unsuccessful efforts to wean drivers off combustion engines, sales of electric vehicles are surging in Europe thanks to the jump in fuel prices stoked by geopolitical upheaval. The U.S.-Israeli war on Iran is disrupting tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, pushing the average price of a liter of gasoline in Germany to a record €2.31 a liter (equivalent to $10 per gallon). Germany, the biggest market, led the gains with a three-quarter jump while sales in France more than doubled.

item.title: Online Insurance Marketplace Insurify Blocks Meta’s Personal AI Agent Muse
item.description: 23, the online insurance marketplace said it was cutting off a different personal AI agent. Meta’s Muse has been blocked from accessing Insurify’s comparison platform because the information the AI agent spits out “risks stripping carrier quotes of critical contextual information that consumers need to make informed insurance-buying decisions,” Insurify said. We support AI agents that make insurance shopping better, but they need to preserve the information and consumer control required to make an informed insurance decision.” The spokesperson said Insurify has no exclusive relationship with ChatGPT, and the decision to block Muse was may not be exclusive either.

item.title: Europe Energy Chief Warns of Growing Risk of Attacks on Infrastructure
item.description: Companies must prepare for successful attacks on critical power infrastructure as both physical and cyber threats continue to increase, the CEO of E.ON, Europe’s largest operator of energy grids, said on Thursday. “Attacks on our grids are increasing significantly,” Leonhard Birnbaum told an industry conference, adding that both physical and cyber attacks had increased in recent years. Birnbaum said companies should abandon the idea that they could fully shield themselves from attacks and rather focus on preparation, pointing to the fact that grid assets are high in numbers and geographically spread.

item.title: Invest in Psychological Capital to Help Employees Manage Increasing Stress
item.description: However, findings from the survey reveal that organizations can help their workers manage stress and change by investing in psychological capital. “Organizations that make the effort to invest in their employees’ psychological capital will be better positioned to succeed in challenging circumstances, rather than being overwhelmed by them.” Much like financial capital, psychological capital is a resource that employers can help their workers cultivate to become more successful and resilient.

item.title: Cargo Theft a Top Concern for Majority of Retail Loss Control Leaders
item.description: A new survey of 150 U.S.-based loss and organized retail crime prevention leaders finds that 81% report it has become more organized in recent years, while 79% say their organization is more concerned about cargo theft than ever before, according to SmartSense by Digi’s Cargo Theft Report. More than half of respondents (63%) said cargo theft incidents have increased compared with last year and 81% said that organized retail crime is a growing concern for their organization. New forms of instantaneous location tracking and visibility intelligence are needed to understand what normal movement looks like, identify anomalies quickly and act before suspicious activity turns into a multimillion-dollar loss.” When asked about cargo theft tactics, respondents identified fraudulent pickups and carrier impersonation (78%), GPS jamming and spoofing (71%), trailer theft (66%), and double brokering (64%) as their top concerns.

item.title: Affordable and accessible reinsurance remains critical to Florida market’s stability: Morningstar DBRS
item.description: Given Florida’s significant exposure to hurricane risk, a new report from Morningstar DBRS has suggested that continued access to affordable and readily available reinsurance will remain critical to the market’s long-term stability and financial strength. “Given Florida’s significant hurricane exposure, continued access to affordable and readily available reinsurance will remain critical to the market’s long-term stability and financial strength.” Morningstar DBRS also stressed that the remainder of the 2026 hurricane season will still be an important test of recent market improvements. Over the longer term, the market’s sustainability will depend heavily on the industry’s ability to generate adequate returns while maintaining coverage that remains accessible and reasonably affordable for Florida residents.” In addition, the report also highlights how reinsurance market conditions in Florida have also drastically improved in recent years, following the stressed environment that it experienced during the height of the Florida market disruption.

item.title: ILS should be seen as a source of ‘strategic possibility’ not just capital: Aeolus’ Dutt
item.description: Aditya Dutt, President of Aeolus Capital Management, has indicated that the re/insurance industry is not making full use of the insurance-linked securities (ILS) investor base by treating the market as just a source of capital, where it should also be viewing it as a source of “strategic possibility”. People who issue stock, nothing against it, but you don’t know who they are, and you can’t pick up the phone and call your shareholders and say, ‘Hey, what do you think of doing this transaction together?’ “And I think the most underutilised aspect of the ILS industry is this notion that it’s a source of capital, and not a source of strategic possibility.” Dutt also added that the size of the investor base in ILS means the opportunity goes well beyond simply offering investors new lines of business. But opening the door to strategic possibility really expands the opportunity set of what we can do.” During the webinar, Dutt also called the role of third-party capital “critical,” saying: “It’s growing, and its capabilities are expanding.

item.title: Reinsurers eye specialty lines to drive growth as property cat rates soften: Berenberg
item.description: Reinsurers are shifting their growth focus from core catastrophe markets toward high-barrier specialty lines as property catastrophe rates face continued softening, according to Berenberg comments following the 2026 Monte Carlo Rendez-Vous de Septembre. Berenberg observed that even though property cat cover is absorbing the market’s steepest rate declines – which in part reflects its profitability since 2023 -, US property cat remains attractive for reinsurers. Outside traditional cat lines, reinsurers’ focus for growth includes speciality lines and, within speciality lines, construction and engineering risks, as well as credit and surety.

item.title: Singapore Court Strips Control of Radiant World From Founder
item.description: A Singapore court appointed KPMG restructuring executives to take charge of Radiant World on Thursday, granting an application by creditor Mizuho Bank Ltd., which has accused the trader of alleged fraud linked to iron ore receivables. The decision removes Radiant World founder Pinkesh Nahar’s control over the group’s key operating entity, opening a new chapter in a saga that has gripped the global commodities industry since Bloomberg first reported in July on concerns that it had been using falsified documents to raise money from banks. KPMG executives Toh Ai Ling, Adrian Chan and Tan Yen Chiaw will be interim judicial managers of Radiant World Corporation Pte., the trader’s key operating entity in Singapore, according to people familiar with the court’s decision, which was communicated on Thursday.

item.title: The Investigation Referral Is Not an Order Form
item.description: When a referral is treated like an order form, everyone may complete exactly what was requested and still fail to answer the most important question. View Series A referral may say, “Conduct two days of surveillance,” “Locate and interview the witness,” or “Complete a social media investigation.” Those instructions identify a service, but they do not always explain the question the investigation is supposed to answer. An investigative referral should authorize the work, but it should also begin a conversation.

item.title: ILS can play a broader role in narrowing the global protection gap: Moody’s
item.description: All of which leads Moody’s to turn attention towards ILS, and how the market can play a key role in helping narrow the gap. As the severity and frequency of natural catastrophe events continue to grow, addressing the protection gap remains an important focus, which has led Moody’s to call out that scaling the capital markets and tapping into the insurance-linked securities market can help narrow the gap as it continues to grow. In a recent article published by Moody’s, the firm outlines that property and casualty (P&C) insurers and reinsurers cannot close the protection gap on their own, stating that they must charge enough premium to pay claims, stay within regulatory capital requirements, whilst also generating returns for shareholders.

item.title: Nascent Re issues $20m Quinton, $20m Stevenage preferred share insurance-linked securities
item.description: a licensed reinsurance transformer owned and operated by Bermuda-based Nascent Group, has completed issuance of two more series of preferred share private insurance-linked securities (ILS), with the vehicle issuing $20 million each for Quinton and Stevenage segregated accounts. All $40 million of preferred shares from the Quinton and Stevenage segregated accounts of Nascent Re have been privately placed with qualifying investors and have now been listed on the Bermuda Stock Exchange (BSX) as insurance-linked securities. The first issuance of listed insurance-linked securities from Nascent Re came to light earlier this year in March, with a €10 million tranche of OFS Re Series 2026-001 preferred shares issued .

item.title: Summer storms across the Canadian Prairies caused over $1.8bn in insured losses: CatIQ
item.description: Ten extreme weather events impacted the Canadian Prairies this summer, causing widespread damage and over $1.8 billion in insured losses, according to initial estimates from CatIQ. Between June 9th and 10th over $900 million in insured losses in Saskatchewan and Manitoba were caused by a series of severe storms that brought tornadoes, hail, damaging winds, torrential rain and flash flooding to communities across both provinces. Between June 20th and 21st, prolonged rainfall caused extensive flooding in Edmonton and the surrounding area, which caused over $160 million in insured losses, While between the 26th and 30th, all three provinces were impacted by a slow-moving storm which moved across the Prairies, causing extensive flooding with Canmore and Kananaskis County, Alberta declaring local states of emergency.

item.title: Tesla’s Automated Driving System Often Misreads Speed Limits: Belgian Safety Group
item.description: Tesla’s FSD automated-driving system frequently exceeded speed limits and attempted to overtake cyclists on streets where it’s prohibited, a road-safety advocacy group said, citing tests it conducted in Belgium. The Belgian group Johanna.be – which advocates for pedestrian and cyclist safety – tested Tesla’s system over three days in July, covering about 400 km (249 miles). It found that FSD often exceeded speed limits in 20 km/h and 30 km/h zones, and incorrectly displayed higher speed limits to drivers, potentially misleading them about how fast the vehicle should travel.

item.title: OpenAI Agent Hacked Australian Government Health Website
item.description: An OpenAI model hacked an Australian government website earlier this year, marking one of the first known cyberattacks by artificial intelligence on a government database. An attack on a government brings new focus to that risk, after a series of incidents this summer in which OpenAI models broke into online resources of outside companies, most notably with the case of Hugging Face , a website hosting AI datasets. The government is also concerned about how it took months for OpenAI to inform Canberra about the incident, Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles said.
